---
title: "The deck engine"
---

`format: revealjs` renders to a slide deck driven by qmd-fast's **own** engine, not
reveal.js. The engine is two bundled assets, `assets/css/deck.css` and
`assets/js/deck.js`, emitted inline by `render/deck.rs`. Three decisions shape it:

- **A native DOM contract.** The markup is `.qmd-deck > .qmd-slides > section`
  (each slide a `.qmd-slide`, with nested `<section>` stacks). Per-slide visibility
  is the camera transform itself, not state classes. The public JS surface is
  `window.QmdDeck` (`initialize` / `sync` / `slide` / `on` / `getSlides` /
  `getCurrentSlide` / `registerPlugin`, …), which the preview client and theme
  extensions bind to.
- **Bundle everything offline.** `deck.css` / `deck.js` (and KaTeX, the `{js}`
  enhancer, highlight CSS) are `include_str!`'d into the page. No CDN, no network.
- **Reuse the block model.** Every slide's blocks still carry `data-block-id` +
  `data-sourcepos`, so the block diff, click-to-source, and live execution work in a
  deck exactly as on a page, *within the current slide*.

## From document to slides

Give `post.qmd` a `format: revealjs` line and the very same three blocks become a
one-slide deck: the `# Cooling coffee` heading opens the slide, with the math and
the live plot riding along unchanged. The deck is built from the same block list as
every other output, and `render/deck.rs` groups those blocks into slides:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  blocks["block list<br/>(data-block-id + sourcepos)"] --> split["split_slides<br/>## → slide, # → section stack, --- → break"]
  split --> dedup["dedup_slug<br/>distinct section ids"]
  dedup --> thread["heading-attribute threading<br/>{background-* / auto-animate} hoisted onto &lt;section&gt;"]
  thread --> emit["deck_page_from_doc<br/>inline deck.css/js (+ KaTeX / {js} enhancer when present)"]
```

- **`split_slides`** walks the blocks: a level-2 heading opens a slide, a level-1
  heading opens a *section* whose following slides become a vertical stack, and a
  `---` rule is an explicit break. Each slide gets an id from its heading text,
  deduped (`step`, `step-1`, …) so repeated titles, common with auto-animate, don't
  collide in the DOM or the URL hash.
- **Heading-attribute threading.** Authors write per-slide options on the heading
  (`## Title {background-color="#0f172a" auto-animate=true}`). The renderer lifts
  those onto the `<section>` as `data-background-*` / `data-auto-animate`, where the
  runtime reads them.

## The runtime (`deck.js`)

A single `deck` state object holds the position (`h`, `v`, `f`: horizontal,
vertical, fragment step), the mode, and the plugin/listener registries. The core
loop is small:

- **`layout`** scales the fixed 960×540 (16:9) stage to the viewport with a single
  CSS transform (`--qmd-deck-scale`), so slides never reflow; `fitSlide` shrinks a
  slide's own font if its content overflows (PowerPoint-style autofit).
- **`apply`** makes exactly one slide visible (inline `display` so an extension's
  `!important` can't leak other slides in), runs its per-slide effects, and records
  the previous slide for transitions.
- **Navigation** (`right`/`left`/`down`/`up`, plus keyboard and touch) moves through
  the step list, then across slides.

### One step list per slide

Fragments, code line-stepping, and magic-move all advance with the same key, so they
share one ordered step list. `fragsOf(slide)` returns step descriptors in document
order:

- `{frag: el}`: an incremental list item or `.fragment`.
- `{code: pre, seg}`: the next segment of a `code-line-numbers` block.
- `{mm: div}`: the next snapshot of a `.magic-move` block.

`deck.f` is how many steps have been taken; advancing dispatches to the matching
handler. Magic-move and auto-animate animate with **FLIP** (measure First and Last
rects, Invert with a transform, Play), scale-corrected by `--qmd-deck-scale` so the
motion is right inside the scaled stage.

### Modes

One engine, several presentations, selected by a `?qmd=` query param or a class:

| Mode | Trigger | What it does |
|------|---------|--------------|
| normal | (default) | the interactive deck |
| speaker | `S` → popup at `?qmd=speaker` | current + next slide previews, notes, timer |
| embed | `?qmd=embed` | passive preview (no key/scroll capture); used by speaker previews and `{{< embed >}}` |
| overview | `Esc` / `O` | zoomed grid of all slides |
| print | `Ctrl/Cmd-P` / `?qmd=print` | flattened, one slide per page |
| scroll | narrow screen / `?qmd=scroll` | a single scrollable reading column |

Speaker view and the audience window stay in sync over `postMessage` (it works on
`file://`, unlike `BroadcastChannel`). When the deck flattens (overview, scroll,
print), the per-slide background layer is hidden and the light-on-dark text class is
cleared, so a dark slide stays readable instead of going white-on-white.

## Embedding a deck

`{{< embed deck.qmd >}}` (see [Slides, books & sites](../guide/using/formats.html)) is a
built-in shortcode in `render/extension`. It emits an iframe to the referenced
deck's built `.html` plus a fullscreen button; the iframe is the isolation boundary
that keeps the deck's full-viewport CSS, global keyboard handler, and URL hash from
fighting the host page. The build and preview discover embed targets
(`embed_targets`) and render each referenced deck to its own self-contained page, so
the iframe resolves without the deck also becoming a navigable site page.
